bullets.title: AAPL: Citi reiterates Buy/$365 PT on resilient iPhone 18 Pro/Max Week 1 demand
bullets.body: Citi's Innovation Lab tracked iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max delivery times across US, China, India, and UK in Week 1 — times slightly higher in US/UK vs. prior year, consistent in India, shorter in China (longest at ~4 weeks Pro/~5 weeks Pro Max). Citi maintains Buy with $365 PT (33x FY28 P/E, 8.6% total return), citing margin expansion, services mix, and Apple Intelligence adoption. Separately, Apple agreed to DRAM at $2.0/GB (up from $1.50) and NAND at $0.33/GB (up from $0.26) for 1Q27, pressuring iPhone margins with no relief through 2028.

bullets.title: NFLX: Wells Fargo downgrades to Underweight, cuts PT to $57 on content/churn risk
bullets.body: Wells Fargo cut NFLX to Underweight from a prior rating and slashed its price target to $57 from $80. The firm sees Top 100 original hours declining YoY, a weaker H2 2026 original content slate, elevated churn risk in 2027, and lower margin expansion in 2027-2028. Stock down ~4.4% pre-market on the news.

bullets.title: META Muse hits #1 App Store; agentic commerce thesis gains traction with $30tn TAM
bullets.body: Meta's new AI app Muse reached the #1 spot on the US Apple App Store and has been in the top 5 downloads for 9 straight days. MS and consumer analysts estimate 100M Muse users could add +1% to 2028 EPS conservatively, with up to +15% upside if transaction/commission monetization materializes against a $30tn consumer spending TAM. MS sees META, SHOP, AMZN, and AAPL as the cleanest agentic winners with scaled distribution and unique datasets.

bullets.title: HUBS Analyst Day: 2030 op margin target raised to 30%; stock -2.9% on growth concerns
bullets.body: HubSpot raised its 2030 long-term non-GAAP operating margin target to 30% from 25% (GAAP 20%), reaffirmed FY26 non-GAAP margin at 21% and FY27 at 23-24%, and launched several AI-native products including agentic accounting and a self-updating CRM. No revenue growth guidance provided, which worried analysts; sell-side consensus is 43% Buy/51% Hold at avg PT $248.97 (8.4% upside). BTIG Buy/$250, Mizuho Outperform/$260, Needham Buy/$300. MS sees the analyst day as reinforcing HUBS's AI moat but prefers to wait at 2x revs for a growth inflection.

bullets.title: INTU Analyst Day: Wolfe Peer Perform; sell-side 58% Buy at $397 avg PT, stock cheap at 13x CY27
bullets.body: Intuit's analyst day focused on re-accelerating new customer growth and scaling Big Bets (>30% of revenue, growing >30%), with long-term targets of 10-15% CAGR for GBSG, 4-8% for Consumer, and high-teens+ NG EPS growth. TurboTax lost ~1pt of IRS e-file share; Business Platform growth slowed to 4%. INTU is down 52% YTD vs IGV flat and trades at 12.5x CY27 P/E vs 21x peer median. Wolfe rates Peer Perform with fair value $300-$400; bullish sell-side (RBC $385, Susquehanna $415, KeyBanc $400) see Big Bets as catalyst; Truist (Hold/$300) treats it as a 'show me' story.

bullets.title: RDDT: DA Davidson trims PT to $185, reiterates Buy; DAU growth tracking below consensus
bullets.body: DA Davidson cut its Reddit price target from $200 to $185 (23x/17x '26/'27 EBITDA) while reiterating Buy, citing DAU Y/Y growth tracking at +12.8% vs. consensus +15.4%. The firm sees mobile web-to-app conversion offsetting DAU weakness to maintain revenue/EBITDA, and flags the Google data licensing deal as unlikely to renew until 1Q27 — stock will be priced as 'no renewal' until that changes.

bullets.title: GOOGL: MS sees stock 'too cheap' ahead of Gemini 4; agentic search headwind acknowledged
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley views GOOGL as 'too cheap' ahead of the Gemini 4 release, which is likely in stealth mode. However, MS's consumer desk flags that if platforms like Meta Muse capture commercial intent at take rates 5-10x lower than current search CPCs, GOOGL search faces a structural traffic and monetization headwind from agentic commerce. MS Hyperscale CDS basket (MSFT/GOOGL/META/AMZN/NVDA) priced at ~65-68bp as modest capex/FCF repricing protection.

bullets.title: TSEM: Barclays initiates Buy/$310 PT; MTSI: BMO upgrades to Buy/$335 PT on optical/aero upside
bullets.body: Barclays initiated Tower Semiconductor at Buy with a $310 PT (30x 2028 P/E), citing siphon revenues growing from ~$330M to ~$2B and near-package optics data center exposure. BMO upgraded MAST Semi to Buy with a $335 PT, modeling ~60% annual EPS growth justified by ~30x P/E vs. current 29x and diversification into aero/defense and satellite. Both names up ~2% pre-market.

bullets.title: COHR: PhotonLink platform unveiled at ECOC; NPO emerges as bridge to CPO
bullets.body: Coherent announced its PhotonLink integrated-optics platform spanning the full optical signal chain at ECOC 2026. NPO (near-package optics) is increasingly positioned as the practical bridge between pluggables and full CPO adoption, consuming ~11W per 800G port vs. ~30W for pluggables and ~9W for CPO. MS revised optical transceiver market upward to $40B-$50B CY26E. MS is hosting investor meetings with CIEN, CSCO, COHR, and NOK at ECOC Sept 20-24.

bullets.title: MARA: MS raises PT to $11 on ERCOT batch progress; CIFR PT to $54; HUT cited as co-beneficiary
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Stephen Byrd raised MARA's PT from $6 to $11 after management expressed conviction to secure HPC data center deals by year-end, which would trigger a framework reassessment with greater upside. CIFR PT raised from $53.50 to $54 following ERCOT Batch Zero conditional classifications at three Texas sites (~4.8GW planned). CIFR and HUT flagged as most likely to execute on PSP grid access + off-grid generation strategies for larger data center campuses.

bullets.title: MU: India packaging ramp underway; CXMT NAND entry seen as early-stage threat
bullets.body: Micron CEO confirmed its Gujarat Surat facility (India's first semiconductor packaging/testing plant) will ramp to tens of millions of units in 2026 and hundreds of millions in 2027. On CXMT NAND: Wolfe and Hedgeye view the China entrant as years away from competitive scale — CXMT HBM3E is only ~1% of capacity by end-2026, yield below 20%, and NAND effort would likely benefit SIMO as a merchant controller customer.

bullets.title: SMCI/DELL: GPU cloud rental prices up 17-21%; server demand accelerating on AI
bullets.body: GPU cloud providers Nebius and CoreWeave raised rental prices 17-21% with short-term power contracts running ~$40M/MW, signaling GPU supply constraints. This is bullish for Server OEM demand, with SMCI and DELL (up 349% YTD, at 52-week high) primary beneficiaries. Liquid cooling content per MW (ETN Boyd) doubled to $3.4M; no data center project pauses or cancellations flagged across five companies in channel checks.

bullets.title: PLTR: Oppenheimer hosting expert call with $100M Lumen customer on platform differentiation
bullets.body: Oppenheimer is running an expert call with Lumen's AI director — a ~$100M annual Palantir customer — covering platform differentiation vs. Databricks, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Oracle; customer expansion dynamics; and product changes over the past 12-18 months. Lee and Ives (via The Compound) flag PLTR as a primary sovereign AI infrastructure beneficiary alongside NVDA.

bullets.title: TSLA: FSD shows 40% fewer collisions in ANZ; Cybercab rides begin at Austin facility
bullets.body: Teslas driving on FSD (Supervised) in Australia and New Zealand experienced 40% fewer collisions on average than non-FSD vehicles. OPCO hosted Cybercab rides at Tesla's Austin facility Sept. 17, with an AUR analyst day and KDK Dallas autonomy event coming Sept. 23-24. Lee/Ives flag Tesla as a primary robotics/physical AI vehicle and assign 80% odds of a Tesla-SpaceX merger by end-2026.

bullets.title: NVDA: Options calls cheap on low IV (<7 IV rank) despite elevated skew; bull thesis intact
bullets.body: With IV ranks at ≤7 and call skew percentiles at +90th percentile, tech calls — especially NVDA — offer attractive risk/reward for bullish positioning. Lee and Ives reinforce the bull case: Nvidia is 2-3 years ahead of Huawei, AI chip demand-to-supply is 13:1, and true equilibrium is unlikely before 2029.

bullets.title: META Connect event next week; MS Week Ahead flags as most notable investor day on calendar
bullets.body: META is holding its Connect developer/hardware event Wednesday-Thursday of next week, flagged by MS as the most notable analyst/investor day in the weekly calendar. This comes as Muse hits #1 in the App Store and agentic commerce debate builds around META's platform advantages.

bullets.title: CHTR: Spectrum Mobile at $30-50/mo across 11M+ homes after Cox integration; AI infra positive
bullets.body: Charter is integrating the Cox acquisition with Spectrum Mobile now priced $30-50/month across 11M+ homes, offering free service for a year and up to $2.5K device financing. Separately, the server demand note views CHTR's advancing AI platforms as a positive.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS: Capital-intensive neo-cloud evaluation framework; CoreWeave raises convertible offering to $3.7B
bullets.body: Analyst commentary highlights CRWV and NBIS as capital-intensive growth businesses best evaluated on CapEx, cash flow, balance sheet, and growth trajectory rather than traditional software metrics. CoreWeave separately upsized its convertible senior notes offering from $3.0B to $3.7B, a sign of robust demand for AI infrastructure financing.

bullets.title: DELL/NET 52-week highs; NFLX, CCL at 52-week lows on StreetAccount scan
bullets.body: StreetAccount's 52-week high/low scan on 9/18 shows DELL up 349% YTD and NET up 48.4% YTD both at highs; NFLX and CCL (down 29.8% YTD) at 52-week lows. Energy dominated highs (9 names); communications and finance dominated lows.

bullets.title: TX data center policy risk: Hinojosa potentially ahead of Abbott in governor poll
bullets.body: New polls show Democratic challenger Hinojosa potentially ahead of Governor Abbott in Texas for the first time. Hinojosa has pushed moratoriums and ending tax breaks for data centers — a material policy risk given Texas is a key pro-data center regulatory environment and a major ERCOT-linked site for MARA, CIFR, and other AI infrastructure names.
